title: AI Infrastructure Will Mint More Millionaires Over the Next Decade: 3 Stocks to Buy Right Now
author: Leo Sun
description: The global AI infrastructure market is projected to expand at 26.6% CAGR through 2034. Three infrastructure leaders—Marvell, Coherent, and Vertiv—are positioned to capitalize on this growth through connectivity chips, fiber-optic components, and cooling systems respectively. All three stocks show strong EBITDA growth projections and are considered reasonably valued relative to their long-term potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company provides essential high-speed connectivity chips and DPUs for AI data centers with projected 44% EBITDA CAGR through 2029. Positioned as a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure expansion.

Leading photonics company experiencing strong demand as data centers replace copper with fiber-optic cables. Expected 44% EBITDA CAGR through 2028 reflects robust growth prospects in AI infrastructure.

Provides critical thermal management and cooling solutions for high-powered AI chips. Co-developing infrastructure with Nvidia and projecting 38% EBITDA CAGR through 2028, indicating solid growth trajectory.
Mentioned as a reference point for AI chipmakers but not the focus of the article. Collaborating with Vertiv on cooling systems, indicating continued importance in the AI ecosystem.

title: 5 Stocks Poised to Outperform With Their Best Growth Still Ahead
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: Five financially strong industrial companies—GE Vernova, Vertiv Holdings, Comfort Systems USA, Sterling Infrastructure, and Powell Industries—are positioned to benefit from AI data center expansion and power grid electrification. Each company has strong balance sheets with low debt and substantial cash reserves, enabling continued investment and growth. However, valuations are elevated and all five are exposed to the same cyclical theme, so a slowdown in data center spending could impact them collectively.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong cash position ($10B+), minimal debt, quadrupled free cash flow, massive backlog ($160B+), and record data center equipment orders indicate robust growth potential in AI infrastructure.
Direct beneficiary of data center expansion with $15B backlog, strong free cash flow generation, modest leverage, and recent investment-grade bond refinancing improve financial flexibility.
50% revenue from data center/technology projects, record-level backlog, $1B+ annual operating cash flow, and light leverage position the company well for continued growth.
Net cash position provides flexibility, backlog jumped over 100%, and major semiconductor campus project indicate strong demand and growth runway.

Fortress balance sheet with hundreds of millions in cash and no drawn debt, nearly 100% surge in new orders, record backlog, and largest data center order in company history ($400M+) signal significant demand acceleration.

title: A Big Bet on Fusion Just Became the First to be Publicly Listed, and it’s making a lot of noise
author: Canada News Group
description: General Fusion Group Ltd. (GFUZ) debuted on Nasdaq as the first publicly listed fusion energy company, rallying approximately 21% on its first trading day. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Jeff Bezos and Tobias Lütke, uses a mechanically-driven Magnetized Target Fusion approach and entered public markets with ~$150 million to fund technical milestones through 2028, including reaching the Lawson criterion for net energy production.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Nasdaq debut with ~21% first-day gain, significant backing from prominent investors, differentiated technical approach, and positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by AI infrastructure buildout. However, company is pre-revenue with significant technical risks ahead.

Strong Nasdaq debut with ~21% first-day gain, significant backing from prominent investors, differentiated technical approach, and positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by AI infrastructure buildout. However, company is pre-revenue with significant technical risks ahead.
Referenced as the root driver of electricity demand through AI accelerators powering data centers, creating urgent need for power solutions that fusion aims to address long-term.
Benefiting from immediate data-center power demand with gas-turbine supply sold out through 2030, representing near-term solution to the same energy demand that fusion addresses long-term.
Strong performer with tens of billions in backlog supplying critical data-center power and cooling infrastructure, benefiting from AI-driven power demand surge.
Thematic cousin to fusion with on-site clean power generation for data centers, validating the core thesis of customer demand for abundant, clean, independent power sources.

title: AI Capex Crosses $1 Trillion Next Year. Here Are 2 Industrial Stocks That Will Benefit
author: Leo Sun
description: As AI spending by U.S. hyperscalers is projected to reach $1 trillion in 2027, industrial companies supporting data center infrastructure are positioned for significant growth. Vertiv Holdings and Quanta Services are highlighted as key beneficiaries, with Vertiv providing thermal management and power systems for AI chips, while Quanta builds transmission infrastructure to support power-hungry data centers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Revenue more than doubled from 2021-2025, adjusted EBITDA tripled, backlog doubled year-over-year to $15B, and analysts expect 28% revenue and 38% EBITDA CAGRs through 2028. Strong partnership with Nvidia positions it well for AI infrastructure growth.

Year-end backlog more than doubled from $19.3B to $44B (2021-2025), driven by cloud and AI market expansion. Analysts expect 17% revenue and 19% EBITDA CAGRs through 2028. Positioned to benefit from grid upgrades and renewable energy infrastructure buildout.
Mentioned as a partner to Vertiv and driver of demand for infrastructure upgrades due to power-hungry AI chips, but not the primary focus of the investment thesis.

title: 2 Top Power Stocks That Could Outperform the Market Through 2030
author: John Ballard
description: As AI data centers require massive power infrastructure investments (estimated at $6 trillion by 2030), two companies are positioned for significant growth: Vertiv Holdings, which supplies cooling and power management systems with 30% YoY revenue growth, and GE Vernova, a gas turbine supplier with a $163 billion order backlog. Both stocks have already surged this year and are expected to continue outperforming the market through 2030.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 30% YoY revenue growth accelerating during AI boom, robust pipeline, raised full-year guidance (29-31% growth expected), deep relationships with hyperscalers, and McKinsey estimates of $6 trillion data center investment by 2030 support continued outperformance potential.

Massive 71% YoY order backlog growth ($163 billion), supplies 25% of world's electricity, 16% YoY revenue growth, and Goldman Sachs projects 165% rise in data center power demand by 2030, positioning the company for substantial earnings growth and long-term profitability.
